speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This year's debate comes at a major turning point in our nation's history.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Our achievements over the past 50 years have given us plenty to cheer about, but the challenges ahead remind us that we cannot take these successes for granted.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In his Budget Statement, the Minister for Finance said that, "Budget 2016 is the beginning of a journey towards SG100." The focus is squarely on the future and getting there together.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The emphasis of this Budget is on economic transformation and building a more caring and resilient society.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Over the past nine days, many echoed the Finance Minister's call for this twin spirit of enterprise and care for one another.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We can all pat our backs and claim that we have improved productivity in this Chamber.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: A key focus of last year's Budget was to help Singaporeans upgrade their skills and achieve retirement adequacy.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: My Ministry, the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY), though coming in second, topped the list on total speech time for the cuts filed, the first time in the short history of MCCY.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This reflects Members' interest in community building and the "softer" side of nation-building, which has clearly taken on greater emphasis in this post-SG50 year.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Even as we look ahead to build Singapore's future economy, we are also asking ourselves how we can better tackle challenges on the social front – preparing for an ageing society and building a united and resilient people.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Members discussed at length about preparing our industries and our workforce for the future economy.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This theme of transformation continues from previous Budgets, but has taken on renewed emphasis.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Committee on the Future Economy is looking ahead and studying long-term trends to chart the way forward for our economy.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: MOM has shared how it will help Singaporeans and industries "Adapt and Grow" and ensure our workforce remains competitive globally.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) is preparing our young by expanding SkillsFuture and helping them to make better career choices.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry is empowering our industries to create more value through the Industry Transformation Programme.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We are supporting our small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to automate, seizing new opportunities for growth, such as in robotics, leveraging productivity-boosting technology to become more manpower-lean.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We are encouraging the use of new technologies to reduce labour demands in the construction sector.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This use of technology extends to non-economic sectors, too: security Page: 59 cameras for law enforcement; automated clearance facilities at our airports and land checkpoints, better defence technologies; digital technology to enhance access to Government information and e-services.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Thirdly, the debates reminded us that we live in an era of "troubled peace".

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Singapore is not immune to global terrorism and the repercussions of geopolitical instability, both near and far, such as the ISIS, the tensions in the South China Sea or the Middle East conflict.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To stay on top of the evolving security threats and safeguard our sovereignty, we need to strengthen the capabilities of our Home Team and the Singapore Armed Forces, but we also need the community to be vigilant.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We must continue to build a cohesive, resilient and rugged society by strengthening racial and religious harmony and through initiatives like outdoor adventure education and the Outward Bound School.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Fourthly, as we forge ahead to achieve stronger competitiveness, we must also ensure that we move together as one.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This is in keeping with the spirit of our national anthem, "Majulah Singapura", that we progress together as a nation.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The theme of inclusivity cuts across various Ministries.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We are improving our civil and criminal justice system to ensure fair access.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The Ministry of Communications and Information's Smart Nation movement will be an inclusive one, encompassing the needs of the elderly and persons with special needs.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: MOE, too, will be enhancing support for children with special education needs.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: And the Ministry of Social and Family Development is embarking on the third edition of the Enabling Masterplan and more support for unwed mothers.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In this Budget, we are partnering Singaporeans across the whole-of-Government to achieve a brighter future.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We are working with the community to strengthen vigilance through programmes like SG Secure.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We are involving industry players to develop transformation maps for each sector, including making Smart Nation a reality.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We need parents, students and employers to join us in order to achieve holistic education with less emphasis on grades.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For the Fresh Start Housing Scheme to benefit families with children, we need families to commit to stable employment, managing their finances and ensuring that their children attend school regularly.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: MOH's dementia-friendly communities will activate community volunteers to be trained and help look out for persons with dementia.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Several of them made their debut speeches over the past nine days, including the NMPs who were sworn in on the day of the Budget debate.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The learning curve was steep but they have picked up very quickly the official jargons and acronyms, which, I confess, can be confusing even to multi-term MPs like me.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Members in this House would agree with me that we have heard many impactful speeches, with robust and discerning arguments.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They have added to the quality of our debates and enabled this House to scrutinise Budget 2016 thoroughly and holistically.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: On behalf of the House, we thank you and your Deputies for so ably presiding over the sessions and holding the debate proceedings to high standards.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We also wish to thank the staff of the Secretariat in Parliament for their wonderful assistance and support.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Page: 60 There are also people who are not present in this House that I wish to acknowledge.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They are the hardworking and dedicated officers from the Ministries and agencies who have supported us in the front bench; the members of the media who have brought the debate on our policies to Singaporeans.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We have a full agenda ahead of us and much work to do.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Will we still be a shiny red dot in the next 50 years?

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This will depend not just on this House, or the Government, but the whole of Singapore.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: That is how we build a stronger, better Singapore that we can all be proud to call Home.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Transform, indeed, we must if we are to stay relevant to the fast-changing economic, sociopolitical and security environment both locally, regionally and globally.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: As the Minister for Defence put it very aptly, we are now in a new normal period of "troubled peace" and, I must add, not just from the security angle alone.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: There will be disruptions, some pretty serious ones, as many Members noted, as we transform.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Many Members cheered the slew of industry transformation programmes for SMEs outlined in the Budget to spur the transformation of enterprises and industries through innovation.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: But there were also very strong calls for changes and adaptation on the part of our people and workers, too.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Many Members were concerned with loss of livelihoods through skills obsolescence due to automation and strongly welcomed SkillsFuture and stronger measures to support professionals, managers and executives.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Whilst skills obsolescence was a fear previously faced by low-skill, blue-collar workers, it is now more pervasive among middle-income, white-collar workers, where the impact of job losses will be much greater and re-employment a lot tougher without effective labour market intervention.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Listening to the debate, I cannot help wondering whether there are two labour markets running in parallel.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: One covers the traditional sectors like cleaning, security and landscaping, jobs that will always be with us and which are still bedevilled by low wages, poor working conditions and lack of career opportunities.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Running in parallel are sectors that are better able to leverage technology, such as finance, technology and fintech, that promise better pay, better careers and a brighter future.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Members were rightly concerned that if we fail to transform the low-wage jobs, our society will become more fragmented as the income disparity widens.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: This Budget is also special and will be remembered as one that slayed not one but two sacred cows that Members have been raising in this Chamber for a long time: the Primary School Leaving Examination grading system and extended maternity leave for unmarried mothers.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: It reflects a Page: 61 transformational shift in policy aimed at placing children at the heart of what we do, instead of focusing narrowly just on academic excellence or procreation.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Members welcomed the efforts to strengthen our social safety net through schemes, such as Silver Support, but also reminded us on the need for fiscal prudence and sustainability, a difficult balance.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: But supporting our seniors or the lower-income is not a zero-sum game.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: In helping to uplift them, we are also helping to stimulate the economy as they are also consumers.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Giving them hope will not only contribute to a more humane and compassionate society but will also strengthen social cohesion, giving greater legitimacy to our economic programmes and achievements.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: As a Business Times article said, "Keep looking up – the economy depends on it." I counted that in this Budget, 22 new schemes were introduced, including Trade Associations and Chambers-Collaborative Industry Projects (TAC-CIP), Human Capital Partnership (HCP), Global Trader Programme (GTD), Early Admissions Exercise (EAE), Industry Preparation for Pre-Graduates Programme (iPREP), Social Service Fellowship (SSF), Our Singapore Fund (OSF) and many more.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Can you remember at least five of them, hon Members?

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Or at least five of the existing schemes?

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: I must admit that I struggle quite a bit and I do not blame the public if they, too, have a hard time remembering.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: I want to thank all Members for your support and cooperation in helping to bring this debate to a successful conclusion.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Members did well in keeping to the time allotted to them.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Some continued to make lightning speeches, much to the chagrin of our poor interpreters.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: I am glad that I did not have to use the guillotine on any Member during this debate.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Such debates demand much serious thought and reflection from Members and I am glad that most lived up to it.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Members argued well for their pet causes with speeches peppered with facts and figures, but some spoke from their heart and touched us quite profoundly.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: So, Miss Chia Yong Yong, you almost made me cry with your speech!

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: This House may have been built from brick and mortar but not the people inside it.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: We reflect the pain, concerns, joy, aspirations and hopes of the ordinary people whom we represent.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Our debates may not be filled with the sound and fury found in some parliaments but they are, nevertheless, of a high quality.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: My only regret is that not many Singaporeans follow the debate, which is a rich source of information and provides good insights into our policies.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: I went on two house visits during the last two weeks, including one last night, and almost all the residents did not follow the debate.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: How to motivate and empower people to be more interested in what is going on so that they can make informed choices and better decisions for themselves?

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: It can act as a catalyst, it can prod, nudge, persuade and influence, but, beyond that, it really depends on all of us how fast we want to run and how much of that rainbow we want to catch.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: On that note, please allow me to thank the Leader of the House and the Whip and their respective Deputies for their assistance in ensuring a smooth Budget debate.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: I also wish to thank my two able Deputies Mr Charles Chong and Mr Lim Biow Chuan for their support.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Further, I wish Page: 62 to thank the Clerk of Parliament, her Deputy and assistant clerks, reporters, interpreters and the many staff working in the background for their commitment and diligence in carrying out their various duties.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Now, hon Members, I think I should guillotine myself.
